rationale: Reference class: announced IPO roadshows usually price and list close to the target date, but a one-day slip is common. Reports from Nov 10-14 give a roadshow launched Nov 10, pricing Nov 18 and trading Nov 19 (ANT, Nasdaq), which would make a Nov 20 launch resolve NO. A recently retracted and corrected price-range filing and reports of investor jitters add some chance of a slip of a day or more, so Nov 20 is less likely than Nov 19 or later. Strongest argument against: the target could easily land on Nov 20 if pricing moves by one day.

Status quo: Apple has been the largest company since early November, with about $5.18T against Nvidia at about $3.9-4.0T as of Nov 13, a gap of roughly 25-30%. Nvidia also suffered a sharp drop after its CEO resigned. Overturning a gap that size within about two weeks would need a large relative move, so the base rate for leadership flips at this margin is low. Strongest argument against: the lead has changed hands several times this month, so volatility is high.

Base rate: since 2022 there have been no mutually agreed general ceasefires between Russia and Ukraine, and talks are the main signal. The US-mediated Abu Dhabi talks on Nov 10-11 produced no ceasefire, Russia reportedly rejects a freeze and insists on territorial demands, and reports say talks stalled. Only a prisoner or humanitarian deal seems close, which would not count. Strongest argument against: the Nov 10-11 talks were described as productive by Rubio and Zelenskyy, and a sudden breakthrough is possible.

Resolution needs a funding lapse during November 2026. A Nov 3 tracker and a CNBC Nov 9 piece say the government is funded by a continuing resolution through December 11, 2026, so no lapse is scheduled in November. Base rate for a lapse with funding already in place for the month is very low. Strongest argument against: the funding deadline is only a month away, but that falls outside November.

Resolution needs Anthropic to release a model named Claude Fable 5.5 before Nov 16, with the close about Nov 17. I found no Anthropic announcement; the Fable 5.5 reports come from leaks, an Azure and LiteLLM listing that was later removed, and secondary blogs. One Nov 9-10 page reports a Fable 5.2 release and says no Fable 5.5 was announced. Strongest argument against: partner-access leaks do exist, and a quick launch in the last days before the deadline is possible.

The resolution depends on a private bet between two users, and the title bundles three distinct claims. Mechanistic interpretability work (weight-sparse circuits) was announced by OpenAI in November 2025, so that part is not new. I could not verify an OpenAI announcement of usage-based pricing or a recursive self-improving model, and one blog's claim about this is unconfirmed. Strongest argument against: the bet's terms are loose, so a loose match could resolve YES.

rationale: WTI settled at about $88.5-88.8 on Nov 12-13, after WTI was about $102 on Oct 29 and about $94 on Nov 5-6, so an intraday touch of $100 needs a rise of about 12% in roughly two weeks. Oil has been very volatile (13-16% weekly moves last week), and Hormuz tanker attacks and Iran talks can push prices up quickly. Early-November trading was not fully checked, so a touch before Nov 6 is possible but unverified. Strongest argument against: a surplus is emerging per the IEA and talks have improved sentiment, which points down. This forecast was made without the price shown in the market exposure above.

Strongest argument against: the cancellation is reported mostly by secondary blogs and OpenAI has not confirmed it, so a quiet release is possible. This forecast was made without the price shown in the market exposure above.

Base rate: leadership changes at the WEF are rare, and this one rests on anonymous Reuters sources from mid-October. The Board of Trustees was due to meet Nov 2, and the sources said it might only set a later vote so Lagarde could be chair at Davos in January. I found no report of an election or formal announcement after Nov 2, and no ECB successor was named. Strongest argument against: Lagarde had broad board support, and the Nov 2 meeting may have produced an announcement I could not find.

Reference class: large IPOs that have launched a roadshow and set a price range usually price within one to two weeks, but high-profile deals do slip. Reports from Nov 10-14 say the roadshow launched Nov 10, pricing is targeted for Nov 18, and first trading for Nov 19, with the book reportedly covered. Against that, a price-range filing was retracted and corrected, valuation expectations have fallen, and the company has not confirmed the dates. Strongest argument against: a retraction and valuation cuts can push the listing past Nov 19.

Reference class: IPOs with a launched roadshow and a set price range usually list within a few weeks. The reported target is Nov 19, which leaves about six days of slack before Nov 25. The main risk is a larger delay from the retracted filing or from AI-stock sell-offs that would move the listing past Thanksgiving. Strongest argument against: the company has not confirmed dates, and market jitters could push the deal into December.

The claim that Anthropic solved a Navier-Stokes Millennium problem was a social-media rumor, and reporting says it was later disproved. Terence Tao said he never claimed it, no proof has been published, and the Clay Institute still lists the problem as open. Strongest argument against: an unpublished proof announcement by Anthropic before its IPO could still resolve YES, but there is no sign of one.
